title: Uniqueness of the part containing a point
statement: Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a monochromatic rectangle partition for a function $g : X \to Y \to \alpha$, and let $R, S \in \mathcal{P}$. If some point $p \in X \times Y$ lies in both $R$ and $S$, then $R = S$.
hypotheses_covered: P is a monochromatic rectangle partition for g
R is a member of P
S is a member of P
the point p lies in R
the point p lies in S
replaced:
If $\mathcal{P}$ is a monochromatic rectangle partition for $g$ and a point
$p \in X \times Y$ belongs to two parts $R, S \in \mathcal{P}$, then $R = S$.
